headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: browser/MCP-enabled next-ai-draw-io can ingest and transmit Airflow outputs, while shared network egress creates default-path exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language commands, and Airflow can emit outputs that may be copied into it. That makes instruction-hijacking plausible in default workflows, though not proven. Airflow lacks a browser/MCP surface; the interaction is inferred from B’s ingestion path.
conditions: IF Airflow output is pasted or routed into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs
IF next-ai-draw-io treats imported text or diagrams as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a separate review-only workspace for pasted outputs
Disable MCP connectors not needed for the task
Prefix imported content with explicit 'data only' markers
Require human approval before any tool action
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Airflow and next-ai-draw-io

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and next-ai-draw-io sends content to external model APIs and handles API keys. Even without a shared filesystem, moving Airflow-produced files into B can expose sensitive pipeline data to third-party inference backends. The pairwise leakage path is therefore plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs contain sensitive pipeline data and are opened in next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use any listed external API provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive DAG outputs out of the diagram tool
Use a local-only model backend where possible
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly
Redact file contents before import
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between the tools

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or shared mutable resource. next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances, which reduces contention. Airflow is not runnable here, so the conflict pathway is limited and mostly hypothetical.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF an operator manually shares the same API key or workspace across both
mitigations: Assign separate API keys per tool
Avoid shared output directories
Run only one writer per resource at a time
Document ownership of mutable resources
requires-engineering: add locking for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can take natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, so it may treat Airflow-generated text as authoritative input. Airflow can produce operational outputs that B could render or act on without verification. The pairwise cascade is plausible, but no downstream autonomous action is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airflow output is used as source text for diagrams or commands in next-ai-draw-io
IF B is allowed to transform imported content without a verification step
mitigations: Require a second reviewer for imported facts
Separate source data from rendered output
Add checksum or citation checks before rendering
Limit B to visualization-only mode
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is source-available and broadly networked, while next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and can send content to multiple third-party model providers. If regulated data is processed through B, residency and retention obligations can diverge from Airflow’s orchestration context. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Airflow into next-ai-draw-io
IF the selected model provider stores prompts or files outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Use only approved regional model endpoints
Avoid sending regulated data to B
Review retention settings for each provider
Keep API keys in a dedicated secret store
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
